You read transcripts of Bitcoin videos. For each EXCERPT below, the sentences inside <selected> are a clip
that may be shown on its own. Use the whole excerpt (what comes before and after) to judge the selected words. You do
not know how the clip will be used.

<excerpt label="M" channel="TFTC" video_title="The One Mistake That Cost Trump" published="2026-11-07T15:00" show_date="2026-11-12">I mean, so much of our construction has just been completely hamstrung. by these crazy environmental regulations. And it's also made it impossible, even if projects can actually get built, it's made it impossible to do them quickly. And so a lot of projects, because of that, it makes it so they're not even worth it. Or I should say, it creates so much uncertainty that people aren't sure if it will be worth it so they don't go ahead and do them, right? You see this to a lesser extent. It doesn't have as much to do with regulation. It's just the dynamics of the industry. But we've seen this this year with oil where so many market participants have basically been predicting that the war would get wrapped up. And it obviously hasn't. But they kept thinking, all right, this is wrapped up in a month, maybe 60 days, maybe 90 days. And then energy prices will come down as energy markets normalize. Well, if that's the case, it doesn't make sense for me to start operating a well that's profitable at $100, does it? Because I'm not anticipating it's going to still be, the oil is still going to be at 100 when I get this thing running. Furthermore, it doesn't instantly pay itself off, right? I need to operate this for a number of years. And so if I have to run it for several years and I'm going to be running it at a loss, it's not worth it. I'm just not even going to tap that well in the first place. You see the exact same thing because of regulation in countless industries throughout the economy. And because I can't respond quickly enough, there might be a window. Let's say I can turn that oil well on and off with like a day's notice. <selected>Well, in that case, it makes it very easy to adapt to these volatile price conditions.</selected> That's kind of a rough parallel to what you see in a lot of instances throughout the economy, where people look at the regulatory environment and they say, I can no longer, I can't be a nimble business anymore. I can't respond quickly to changing market conditions. And therefore, I don't want to risk running into one of those periods where I lose my shirt and I just don't have the flexibility to change. Okay. So that's, yeah, that's, that's the kind of energy side. The finance side is another big one. And, you know, look, the Fed has a big role to play here. I think the new Fed under Warsh is, let me put it this way. I think Mickey Bowman is free to actually do the right thing now. She's not getting strong armed. into doing all this woke nonsense. And I mean, if you look at the capital requirements that they had previously proposed, not the new ones, but the previous ones, they had all kinds of ridiculous requirements there that had nothing to do with default risk, which is what your capital requirements are supposed to be there to help protect against.</excerpt>

For each excerpt answer:
- "speaker_changes_inside": does the speaker change inside the selected words? "yes" / "no" / "uncertain"
- "view": whose view the selected words express: "own_sincere" (the speaker's own sincere assertion), "attributed"
  (someone else's view, quoted or reported), "hypothetical", "conditional" (true only under a condition), "sarcastic",
  "question", "reading_aloud" (reading a post or article), "ad_read", "joke", or "uncertain"
- "referents": every pronoun or pointing word in the selected words (it, they, this, that, he, she, today, here...)
  that points at something specific, with what it refers to; "inside": true if the selected words themselves give
  its antecedent or the predicate that completes it (an ellipsis completed by an earlier selected sentence: "It's not
  Bitcoin that's getting hacked. It's other intermediaries." = other intermediaries are getting hacked), or it points
  only at a general topic the clip presupposes; "inside": false if a listener needs the words before or after the
  selection; "changes_assertion": "yes" if resolving it differently would change WHAT THE SPEAKER ASSERTS, "no" if
  not, "uncertain". Leave out words that point at nothing outside: a dummy "it" ("it's raining", "it's not X that
  ...", where X is in the selection), and a generic "we" / "you" / "they" meaning people in general
- "conditions": any condition or time frame that governs the selected words, and whether it is INSIDE them
- "retraction": "none", or what the speaker later in the excerpt retracts or qualifies about the selected words
- "time_ok": "yes" if every time word in the selected words (today, now, this week, just, recently, a "current"
  price) still holds on the show date given when the video was published (both on the excerpt), or there is none;
  "no" if it is stale; "uncertain"
- "proposition": in one sentence, what the speaker asserts in the selected words, read in context
- "certainty": "certain", "likely", "possible", "speculative" or "uncertain"
- "speaker_is": "host" if the excerpt shows that the speaker of the selected words is the channel's own host,
  "guest" if it shows a guest or another person speaking them, "uncertain" otherwise; "speaker_evidence": the exact
  words of the excerpt that show it (copied exactly, e.g. the host's own "welcome back to my channel"), or ""
